Recovery WAS assessed, repeatedly and explicitly: (i) rats, full time course - "Acute inhibition response scores were assessed at 30 min to 2 weeks after 700 ug of ASO1 delivered via IT administration in rats (Fig. 1B)... By 16-24 h and for the next 2 weeks, all animals scored a 0, confirming acute inhibition is transient with no long-term sequelae"; (ii) the mouse ICV ASO2-8 panel these rows come from - "Following a single 100 ug ICV injection in mice, the acute inhibition response at 3 h post-injection varied from 0 to 5, depending upon the sequence tested (Fig. 2A), and resolved by 24 h"; (iii) abstract, across species - "inhibition-like responses peaked ~3 h post-ASO delivery, reversed within 24 h with no sequelae"; (iv) rat electrophysiology re-recorded at 24 h - "All MMEP recovered by 24 h after dosing"; (v) Discussion - "The acute inhibition response peaks around 3 h post-administration and is typically fully reversible by 24 h post-dose, with no identifiable sequelae."

summary: 60 rows, 18 sources, grouped and adjudicated source-by-source: 28 CONFIRMED, 3 CONFIRMED_MINOR, 27 REFUTED, 2 UNVERIFIABLE. The standing lead is CONFIRMED and is the largest correction available. In the mouse ICV acute-tolerability panel of doi:10.1089/nat.2021.0071 (Hagedorn 2022) the animals were observed for ONE HOUR and never re-examined; the paper's only recovery language ('waned anywhere between 2 and 4 h post-dose... From 24 h and out to 7 days, we almost never observed any acute behavior reappearing') is expressly tied to 'an initial set of 9 ASOs' - the following sentence, 'Also, for this initial set, mice were injected with doses ranging from 12.5 to 200 ug', pins it. All 18 'reversible' rows from that source are REFUTED to not_assessed. The two 'irreversible' rows survive on a different footing: they score exactly 20.0, the scale anchor the paper defines as euthanasia, which is a property of the score recorded for those very animals rather than prose about other ones. The MIRROR lead is REFUTED: doi:10.1016/j.omtn.2025.102692 (Kuroda 2025) does have a post-dose window - a single injection followed by serial scoring to day 7-21 - and reports that the toxicity 'appeared at least 3 days postinjection, persisted for 6 days or more, and worsened over time', while reporting resolution elsewhere where it occurred ('acute toxicity from ASO2 resolved completely within 1 day'). Its 'irreversible' values stand. Beyond the leads, a second systematic error surfaced that the leads did not name: adverse-event INCIDENCE rows - ClinicalTrials.gov adverseEventsModule entries, FDA-label Table 3, the Qalsody EPAR Table 36, and a trial paper's aggregate 94%-any-AE figure - all carry 'reversible' although an incidence table has no outcome field whatsoever; 7 such rows are refuted to not_assessed. Two further single-row refutations: US11851654B2 Table 10, where the patent itself says the score 'remained up to 6 hours' with 50% of animals still affected and 2/6 dead (-> partially_reversible), and the KCNT1 Nat Med patient-1 dystonia, which the paper says 'improved', not resolved (-> partially_reversible).
systematic_issues: 1. IMPORTED CLASS-LEVEL RECOVERY CLAIMS - the flagged tell is real and diagnostic. Every row from doi:10.1089/nat.2021.0071 repeats the identical sentence in notes ('Reversibility: text states signs waned 2-4 h post-dose and acute behaviour almost never reappeared from 24 h to 7 d (Suppl Fig S2A)'), and that sentence describes a 9-ASO pilot cohort, not the 181 scored animals. But the tell must be applied with the source open, not mechanically: doi:10.1016/j.omtn.2025.102692, doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1333, doi:10.1093/nar/gkag057 and doi:10.1016/j.ymthe.2024.10.024 also carry identical boilerplate in every row, and in those four the boilerplate is a faithful paraphrase of a class-level statement the source really does make about the very animals being scored. The discriminating question is not 'is the note boilerplate' but 'does the source's recovery statement cover the scored cohort'. 2. AE-INCIDENCE LOCI CANNOT SUPPORT A REVERSIBILITY VALUE. Seven rows in this sample assert 'reversible' at a locus that structurally cannot contain it: three ClinicalTrials.gov adverseEventsModule entries (the schema has term/organSystem/numAffected/numAtRisk and nothing else), FDA_NDA209531 label Table 3, EMA EPAR Table 36, doi:10.1002/mus.28372's 24.5% CSF-protein-increased AE, and doi:10.1038/s41591-023-02326-3's aggregate 94% any-AE. Where the source does carry a resolution narrative it attaches to individual SERIOUS events, never to the incidence table - and the extractor has in several cases silently promoted 'did not lead to discontinuation' or 'all events were mild or moderate' into 'reversible'. Neither is reversibility. Sweep all clinical/regulatory AE-incidence rows across the dataset for this. 3. GRADE-0 ROWS SHOULD NOT ASSERT REVERSIBILITY. Nine rows in this sample are graded 0 (no signal, or incidence at/below the concurrent control) yet claim 'reversible'. There is no finding to reverse; not_assessed is the correct filler. This is cheap to fix with a predicate. 4. WHERE THE SOURCE HEDGES, THE ROW SHOULD HEDGE. Two rows flattened 'improved' / 'remained up to 6 hours' into 'reversible' when partially_reversible exists in the vocabulary and the source's own contrastive wording elsewhere in the same document shows the hedge was deliberate. Check partially_reversible usage dataset-wide - it appears to be under-used. 5. THE PATENT LANE IS THE STRONGEST LANE HERE. US9605263B2, US10968453B2 and US11851654B2 all publish PAIRED timepoints (3 hour and 8 week FOB; 1/3/6 hour tolerability), so their reversibility values are directly falsifiable and, with one exception, correct. Nothing in this lane needs a wholesale change.
